sights.description: A quiet forest near Lake Hamana whose rounded buildings suggest a medieval European village, with select shops, cafes, and restaurants.

sights.name: 井伊谷城跡
sights.description: Ii family Sengoku castle on a 115-meter hill, now Shiroyama Park overlooking Iinoya and Lake Hamana.

sights.name: 明善記念館
sights.description: Memorial museum on Hamamatsu entrepreneur Kinpara Meizen, showing his Tenryu River flood control and tree-planting work through relics and documents.

sights.name: 西来院
sights.description: Founded in 1428, this temple holds the mausoleum of Tsukiyama-dono, Tokugawa Ieyasu's wife, who was later killed on his orders.

sights.name: 蜆塚遺跡
sights.description: A late-to-final Jomon village from about 3,000-4,000 years ago, with five reconstructed houses, a preserved shell layer, and relocated old homes.

sights.name: 引間城跡（浜松元城町東照宮）
sights.description: A Sengoku stronghold on the present Hamamatsu Castle site, taken by Ieyasu in 1568 and now home to Motoshirocho Toshogu.

sights.name: 静岡大学 高柳記念未来技術創造館
sights.name_en: Shizuoka University Takayanagi Memorial Future Technology Creation Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall exhibiting materials on Kenjiro Takayanagi, who in 1926 first displayed a character on a cathode-ray tube.

sights.name: 浜松八幡宮
sights.description: Ancient shrine linked to Ieyasu's victory prayers, preserving a thousand-year camphor tree designated a city natural monument.

sights.name: 椿姫観音
sights.description: Memorial to Lady Otazu, Hikima Castle's lord who died fighting Tokugawa forces, now marked by camellias and Tsubakihime Kannon.

sights.name: 本田宗一郎ものづくり伝承館
sights.description: Memorial hall honoring Tenryu-born Soichiro Honda, exhibiting early products he made and valuable materials.

sights.name: 天竜二俣駅
sights.description: Headquarters station of the Tenryu Hamanako Railway, preserving a turntable and roundhouse registered as national tangible cultural properties.

sights.name: 高根城址
sights.description: Mountain castle ruins at 420 meters, later a Takeda base, with bailey, turret, and gate restored based on excavations.

sights.name: 頭陀寺城跡・松下屋敷跡
sights.name_en: Zudaji Castle Ruins and Matsushita Residence Site
sights.description: Old temple and former Matsushita residence where young Hideyoshi reportedly served and Ii Naomasa first entered Ieyasu's service.

sights.name: 細江神社
sights.description: Shrine said to ward off earthquakes, begun in 1510 after a tsunami, holding a July boat ritual on Lake Hamana.

sights.name: 三方原古戦場碑
sights.description: Monument to the 1572 battle where young Tokugawa Ieyasu suffered his only and greatest defeat to Takeda Shingen.

sights.name: 浜松市美術館
sights.description: This art museum centers on Oriental arts and crafts, especially 18th- and 19th-century glass paintings, folk pictures, ukiyo-e, ceramics, and Buddhas.

sights.name: 蜂前神社
sights.description: An ancient shrine in Hoda near Mikatagahara stands where Takeda forces supposedly ambushed Tokugawa troops and once held Ii Naotora's signed document.

sights.name: 井伊直親の墓
sights.description: Ii Naochika, betrothed of Ii Naotora and father of Ii Naomasa, was murdered at 27 in 1562; Ii Naosuke donated the lantern before the grave.

sights.name: 猪鼻湖
sights.description: This quiet branch lake connects to Lake Hamana via the Seto channel, with mandarin slopes and pleasure boats from Seto to Kanzanji Onsen.

sights.name: 礫島
sights.description: This small pine-covered island of about 20 ares in Lake Hamana is said to have formed from a stone thrown by the giant Daidaraboshi.

sights.name: 中村家住宅
sights.description: In 1574 Ieyasu's concubine Oman bore Yuki Hideyasu in this Minamoto-line warrior residence, where the placenta mound still remains.

sights.name: 大草山昇竜しだれ梅園
sights.description: About 300 weeping plums, including trees over 100 years old, are trained here like dragons rising to heaven, a nationally rare style.

sights.name: 大草山
sights.description: This 113-meter scenic spot overlooking Lake Hamana is reached from Kanzanji Onsen by the Kanzanji Ropeway, Japan's only over-lake ropeway.

sights.name: 弁天島海浜公園海水浴場
sights.description: Near Imagireguchi, where Lake Hamana meets the sea, this shallow beach has clear water, roofed wooden porches, and views of a red torii.

sights.name: 徳川秀忠公誕生の井戸
sights.description: A well created from the legend that nearby well water was used for Tokugawa Hidetada's first bath at birth.

sights.name: 犀ヶ崖古戦場
sights.description: Cliff where Ieyasu's night raid across a cloth bridge in the Battle of Mikatagahara sent many Takeda troops falling.

sights.name: 井伊谷宮
sights.description: Shrine to Prince Munenaga, revered as a god of learning, beside the Ii family temple Ryotanji.

sights.name: 気賀関所
sights.description: Historic facility recreating Edo-period inspections at Kiga Checkpoint on the Hime Kaido, with costume experiences.

sights.name: 浜松市姫街道と銅鐸の歴史民俗資料館
sights.name_en: Hamamatsu City Hime Kaido and Dotaku Folk History Museum
sights.description: Museum of Hime Kaido relics and a locally excavated Yayoi bronze bell, with a relocated birth hut outdoors.

sights.name: 清瀧寺
sights.description: Temple built by Tokugawa Ieyasu to mourn his eldest son Nobuyasu, named for a clear waterfall on the grounds.

sights.name: 渋川つつじ公園
sights.description: Park with about 4,000 wild Shibukawa azaleas, a prefectural natural monument, at their best from mid to late May.

sights.name: 浜松市秋野不矩美術館
sights.name_en: Hamamatsu City Akino Fuku Art Museum
sights.description: Wooden art museum of Akino Fuku's Japanese paintings of India, entered shoeless to sit on rattan mats.

sights.name: はままつフラワーパーク
sights.description: A 300,000-square-meter botanical garden by Lake Hamana displaying 3,000 plant species throughout the year.

sights.name: 浜松市博物館
sights.description: Museum tracing Hamamatsu history, highlighted by the only letter bearing Ii Naotora's signature.

sights.name: 浜松科学館 みらいーら
sights.description: A hands-on science park with five zones, over 100 exhibits, and one of the prefecture's largest planetariums.

sights.name: 公益財団法人 平野美術館
sights.description: A private art museum in central Hamamatsu holding about 2,000 works, from Japanese painting to contemporary art.

sights.name: 浜名湖オルゴールミュージアム
sights.description: A specialist museum on Ogusayama displaying about 70 antique music boxes and automatic instruments over 100 years old.

sights.name: 猪鼻湖神社
sights.description: A shrine on Shishi Rock between Lake Hamana and Lake Inohana, reached by a vermilion drum bridge.

sights.name: 大福寺
sights.description: An Okuhamanako temple with an Edo stroll garden, traditional natto, and nationally designated cultural properties.

sights.name: 摩訶耶寺
sights.description: Founded in 726, this Okuhamanako temple has a rare Heian-style garden and nationally designated Buddha statues.

sights.name: 佐久間ダム
sights.description: A 150-meter dam on the Tenryu River, among Japan's largest, with an observation deck and a power museum.

sights.name: 二俣城址
sights.description: Castle ruins on a Tenryu River cliff, contested by the Takeda and Tokugawa, now a quiet park with stone walls.

sights.name: 浜名湖体験学習施設 ウォット
sights.description: A hands-on aquarium where visitors can touch Lake Hamana life, with a 120-ton tank and eel feeding.

sights.name: 白倉峡
sights.description: A celebrated gorge on a Tenryu River tributary, with emerald streams, cliffs, and waterfalls along a 1 km path.

sights.name: 浜松市動物園
sights.description: A lakeside zoo keeping about 100 or more species, including Japan's only golden lion tamarins.

sights.name: 龍雲寺
sights.description: A historic Zen temple on the shore of Lake Sanaru, displaying a 4-by-16-meter Heart Sutra, the world's largest.

sights.name: 茶室 松韻亭
sights.description: A Hamamatsu Castle Park teahouse designed by Yoshio Taniguchi, serving matcha or sencha with seasonal sweets.

sights.name: 浜松まつり会館
sights.description: Exhibition hall where Hamamatsu Festival's full-size giant kites and ornate floats can be seen year-round.

sights.name: 浜名湖ガーデンパーク
sights.description: Park on a Lake Hamana peninsula, whose 50-meter tower views the lake and Mount Fuji on clear days.

sights.name: 浜松市楽器博物館
sights.name_en: Hamamatsu City Museum of Musical Instruments
sights.description: Japan's only public musical instrument museum, displaying about 1,500 instruments from around the world.

sights.name: 浜松城公園
sights.description: A green central park in downtown Hamamatsu, famous for about 270 cherry trees and a children's adventure plaza.

sights.name: 浜松城
sights.description: Where Tokugawa Ieyasu built his foothold toward unification, later nicknamed the Success Castle.

sights.name: 中田島砂丘

sights.name: 弁天島海浜公園

sights.name: 秋葉山本宮秋葉神社 上社
sights.description: Considered the head of over 400 Akiha shrines, enshrining the fire god atop 866-meter Mount Akiha.

sights.description: Shizuoka's oldest building, a 600-year-old Rinzai head temple in Okuyama forest with 500 stone arhats.
